gen_risks.description: Network under‑utilisation if build‑out projects fail to take FID, reducing user fees and revenue for the T&SCo.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure firm take‑or‑pay commitments, include penalty clauses, and allow regulator to disallow CapEx for non‑signed projects.
gen_risks.evidence: risk that if one or more of the build‑out projects ... fails to take FID, the network ... will be underutilised (section 4.2.2).

gen_risks.description: Cost overruns on the T&S network construction exceeding the allowed capital allowance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply cost‑sharing factor, regulator caps, rigorous cost assurance and contingency budgeting.
gen_risks.evidence: Eni T&S network construction overruns; any overruns subject to cost sharing, recoup only 40% (section 4.1.3, 5.7.11).

gen_risks.description: Discontinuation of EETH or Protos leading to loss of revenue and stranded assets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include discontinuation agreements with compensation, monitor milestones and enforce performance penalties.
gen_risks.evidence: Discontinuation risk for EETH and Protos (section 5.7.4).

gen_risks.description: Shortfall in the de‑commissioning fund for the T&S network.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated de‑commissioning fund with regular financial reviews and regulator oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: Decommissioning fund shortfall (section 5.7.5).

gen_risks.description: CO₂ leakage from storage sites causing environmental damage and liability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy robust monitoring, sentinel wells, strict operational standards and SCA insurance coverage.
gen_risks.evidence: Government will underwrite high‑impact, low‑probability CO₂ leakage risks via the Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA) (section 1.3).

gen_risks.description: Regulatory changes by Ofgem to allowed revenue or rate of return affecting T&SCo financial model.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure a long‑term regulatory framework with flexibility clauses and periodic review mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: Ofgem sets allowed revenue and reviews it periodically (section 1.3, 4.4.2).

gen_risks.description: Delays in achieving FID and COD increase costs and erode projected benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply PERT/QSRA assurance, maintain a 6‑month COD tolerance, and enforce strict change‑control processes.
gen_risks.evidence: Schedule tolerance of 6 months delay to COD; schedule assurance uses PERT and QSRA (sections 6.4.2, 6.5.3).

gen_risks.description: Limited supplier capacity and capability could cause cost escalation and delivery delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Early supplier engagement, develop supply‑chain capacity, embed contingencies and monitor market conditions.
gen_risks.evidence: Critical success factors include supplier capacity and capability; cost increases linked to supply‑chain issues (section 3.2.1, 4.2).

gen_risks.description: Low UK ETS carbon price makes capture projects uneconomic, threatening financial viability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide revenue‑support contracts (RSA, CfD‑type), monitor carbon price and adjust strike prices as needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Carbon Price is currently too low to incentivise deployment; business models cover difference between strike and reference price (sections 1.2, 4.1.4).

gen_risks.description: Cross‑chain risk: failure of capture projects reduces T&SCo utilisation and revenue.
gen_risks.mitigation: Allocate cross‑chain risk to appropriate parties, use revenue‑support agreements and monitor project progress closely.
gen_risks.evidence: Government underwrites cross‑chain risks; cross‑chain risks outlined in commercial case (sections 1.3, 4.3).

gen_risks.description: Political shift could alter CCUS policy or subsidy levels, affecting project funding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Align contracts with the Subsidy Control Act, maintain ministerial forum engagement, embed flexibility for policy changes.
gen_risks.evidence: Subsidy Control Act 2022 compliance and ministerial forum on CCUS (sections 4.2.5, 2.2.4).

gen_risks.description: Legal risk of non‑compliance with subsidy‑control principles leading to challenges.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct pre‑referral assessments, work closely with SAU, document compliance evidence.
gen_risks.evidence: Assessment of each subsidy scheme will be submitted to the Subsidy Advice Unit (SAU) (section 4.2.5).

gen_risks.description: Stakeholder opposition or safety concerns could delay permitting and construction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Early community engagement, safety communication, and delivery of local benefits programmes.
gen_risks.evidence: Stakeholder engagement and communications approach includes community engagement and safety (section 6.2).

gen_risks.description: Inadequate data sharing between T&SCo, LCCC and DESNZ may impair monitoring and reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define a data‑management strategy, formal data‑sharing agreements and regular audits.
gen_risks.evidence: DESNZ will define a longer‑term data management strategy; overlapping data flows noted (section 6.6).

gen_risks.description: Technical failure of dense‑phase upgrade or injection wells could limit capacity and availability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Detailed engineering design, phased testing, independent technical assurance and contingency engineering.
gen_risks.evidence: Phase 2 includes dense phase upgrades; technical assurance has examined project technical details (sections 2.3.2, 4.3).

gen_risks.description: High‑cost sensitivity could turn the project’s NPV negative under adverse cost scenarios.
gen_risks.mitigation: Perform high/low sensitivity analyses, enforce strict cost controls, and secure additional funding buffers.
gen_risks.evidence: Option 1 NPV could be -£1.0bn in high‑cost scenario; sensitivity analysis shown (section 3.4.2).

gen_risks.description: Potential air‑quality impacts from waste‑to‑energy facilities within the cluster.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply stringent emission controls, continuous air‑quality monitoring and compliance with standards.
gen_risks.evidence: Costs include potential for CO₂ leakage and environmental and air quality impacts (section 1.4).

gen_risks.description: Geological uncertainty of offshore storage sites could affect long‑term storage integrity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct thorough site characterisation, install monitoring and sentinel wells, and develop contingency storage options.
gen_risks.evidence: CO₂ stored in deep geological formations such as depleted fields or saline aquifers; storage capacity in Liverpool Bay (sections 1.1, 2.3.1).

gen_risks.description: Revenue Support Agreement (RSA) top‑up may be required if user fees fall short, stressing exchequer resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure minimum demand commitments, embed demand forecasts in contracts, and cap government top‑up exposure.
gen_risks.evidence: If shortfall in demand ... government will ‘top up’ fees through RSA (section 1.3).

gen_risks.description: Complex multi‑agency governance could cause decision‑making delays and mis‑alignment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain clear governance structures, regular board meetings, defined escalation paths and documented responsibilities.
gen_risks.evidence: Multiple governance forums: NLT, T1B, PB, CCUS Senior Board (section 4.1.4).

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that government (HMG) is exposed to increased costs for Track-1 post-Financial Investment Decision (FID), and that cost pressures are unaffordable within delegated budgets. [Strategic Case risk T1SR1, Section 2.5 'Identify high level potential risks', p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Contractual mechanisms ensure HMG only takes on specific risks where appropriate, with liability limited and counterparties incentivised to control costs; governance mechanisms monitor costs and provide early warning of overruns; contingent liability exposure is accurately monitored.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that the programme does not realise its intended benefits for Track-1. [Strategic Case risk T1SR3, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Projects undergo detailed technical assurance and financial due diligence; projects must meet Initial Conditions Precedent (ICPs) before contracts take effect and Operational CPs thereafter, with LCCC able to terminate and avoid paying for an underperforming project; contractual mechanisms allocate performance-related risk to the private sector; continued engagement with the global Carbon Management Challenge to expand CCUS use and deliver UK trade benefits.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that the post-FID operating model across public and private sector parties will not operate successfully. [Strategic Case risk T1SR4, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: Medium/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Progress of arm's-length bodies' (ALBs') capacity (funding, resource) and capability (knowledge, skills) to operate successfully post-FID is monitored through the Delivery Board; a DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function will be set up between FID and Commercial Operations Date (COD) to mitigate risks to cluster delivery and system integration; readiness-testing mechanisms are in place ahead of FID; FY24/25 funding for the ALBs to fulfil their roles has been secured.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk of an unclear exit path for HMG from its role in the Track-1 commercial framework. [Strategic Case risk T1SR5, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Key planned developments include amendments to the process for granting economic licences, a move toward a competitive allocation process for capture contracts, and evolution of transport & storage business models to reflect an increased private-sector role in managing cross-chain risks; cost-reduction levers (UK ETS pricing, CBAMs) are intended to help cultivate a self-sustaining industry and enable an HMG exit path.
